# Task 1: Exploring Data Types in R
# Theme: Lvyv — The Floating Sky City


```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 1.1 Atomic Types
# -----------------------------

# numeric values
avg_temperature <- 18.7     # degrees Celsius
altitude_km     <- 7.5      # floating height above ground (km)
energy_rating   <- 92.4     # sustainability rating
water_reserves  <- 35.2     # in million liters

# integer values
population      <- as.integer(12000)
watchtowers     <- as.integer(8)
airships        <- as.integer(42)

# logical values
has_magic_crystals <- TRUE
is_allied_empire   <- FALSE

# character values
city_name   <- "Lvyv"
region_name <- "Sky Realm"
city_type   <- "Floating Metropolis"

cat("The city of", city_name, "is a", city_type, "in the", region_name,
    "floating at", altitude_km, "km with a population of", population, "\n")

```


```{r}
# -----------------------------
# 1.2 Vectors
# -----------------------------

numeric_vector <- c(avg_temperature, altitude_km, energy_rating, water_reserves,
                    population, watchtowers, airships)

sequence_vector <- seq(20, 100, by = 5)

set.seed(123)
logical_vector <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), size = 10, replace = TRUE)

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 1.3 Matrix
# -----------------------------

set.seed(42)
lvyv_matrix <- matrix(sample(-50:50, 9, replace = TRUE),
                      nrow = 3, ncol = 3)

rownames(lvyv_matrix) <- c("Tower", "Docks", "Garden")
colnames(lvyv_matrix) <- c("A", "B", "C")

row_means <- rowMeans(lvyv_matrix)
col_means <- colMeans(lvyv_matrix)

lvyv_matrix
row_means
col_means

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 1.4 List
# -----------------------------

lvyv_list <- list(
  city_name = city_name,
  numeric_vector = numeric_vector,
  sequence_vector = sequence_vector,
  logical_vector = logical_vector,
  infrastructure_matrix = lvyv_matrix,
  description = "Lvyv is a floating city sustained by magic crystals and airships, hovering gracefully above the clouds."
)

lvyv_list

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 1.5 Factor
# -----------------------------

econ_levels <- factor(c("high", "medium", "medium", "high", "low", "medium", "high"))
table(econ_levels)

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 1.6 Data Frame
# -----------------------------

lvyv_df <- data.frame(
  sector = c("Central Spire", "Harbor Deck", "Crystal Forge", "Sky Garden",
             "Guild Quarters", "Aviary"),
  visitors_per_day = c(500, 350, 200, 450, 180, 250),
  is_restricted = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE),
  econ_class = factor(c("high", "medium", "high", "medium", "low", "medium"))
)

colnames(lvyv_df) <- c("Sector", "Visitors", "Restricted", "EconClass")

str(lvyv_df)
summary(lvyv_df)

lvyv_df$TrafficLevel <- ifelse(lvyv_df$Visitors > 300, "high", "low")

lvyv_df

```

```{r}

sequence_vector[3]

sequence_vector[2:5]

# Values greater than 20
sequence_vector[sequence_vector > 20]

```

```{r}

```

lvyv_list$description

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 2.3 Investigating the Data Frame
# -----------------------------

# Print first 3 rows

head(lvyv_df, 3)

# Print value at row 4, column 1

lvyv_df[4, 1]

# Print logical column as vector

lvyv_df$Restricted

```

```{r}

# Logical subsetting

df_subset <- lvyv_df[lvyv_df$Visitors > 300, ]
df_subset

```

```{r}

# Subsetting

df_subset_2 <- lvyv_df[lvyv_df$EconClass %in% c("high", "low"), ]
df_subset_2

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 2.4 Handling “Corrupted” Data (Missing Values)
# -----------------------------

df_corrupted <- lvyv_df

df_corrupted[2, 3] <- NA
df_corrupted[5, 2] <- NA
df_corrupted[6, 4] <- NA
df_corrupted

# Total missing values
sum(is.na(df_corrupted))

# Missing values per column
colSums(is.na(df_corrupted))

mean(df_corrupted$Visitors, na.rm = TRUE)

df_clean <- na.omit(df_corrupted)
df_clean

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 2.5 Bonus Challenge
# -----------------------------

max_index <- which.max(lvyv_df$Visitors)
max_index
lvyv_df[max_index, ]

```

# Task 3: Expanding Your Universe

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 3.1. The Quest: Find Your Data
# -----------------------------

# Data from: https://datahub.io/core/population-city?utm_source=chatgpt.com#unsd-citypopulation-year-both

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 3.2. The Import: Load Your Data
# -----------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(readr)

my_real_data <- read_csv("unsd-citypopulation-year-both.csv")

glimpse(my_real_data)
head(my_real_data)
summary(my_real_data)

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 3.3. The Interrogation: Explore with dplyr
# -----------------------------


# Question 1: Which 10 cities have the highest population in the most recent year?

latest_year <- max(as.numeric(my_real_data$Year), na.rm = TRUE)



my_real_data %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year)) %>%
  filter(Year == latest_year, !is.na(Value)) %>%
  select(City, `Country or Area`, Year, Population = Value) %>%
  arrange(desc(Population)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)


# Question 2: Show all records for the city "TOKYO"

my_real_data %>%
  filter(City == "TOKYO")


# Question 3: Create a new column population_millions showing population in millions

my_real_data %>%
  mutate(population_millions = Value / 1e6) %>%
  select(City, Year, population_millions) %>%
  head(10)


# Question 4: What is the average city population for each country?

my_real_data %>%
  group_by(`Country or Area`) %>%
  summarise(avg_population = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_population)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)


# Question 5: How many times does each city appear in the dataset? (Count records per city)

my_real_data %>%
  group_by(City) %>%
  summarise(records = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(records)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

```

# Task 4. Building a “Toolkit” for Your Universe (Functions)

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 4.1. The “Greeting” Function (A Simple Start)
# -----------------------------

welcome_to_my_universe <- function(your_name, universe_name = "Lvyv - Floating City") {
  cat("-------------------------------------------\n")
  cat("Welcome to the Analysis Toolkit for:", universe_name, "\n")
  cat("Report prepared by:", your_name, "\n")
  cat("-------------------------------------------\n\n")
}

welcome_to_my_universe("Anton")

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 4.2. The “Loading” Function (A Good Practice)
# -----------------------------

load_and_inspect <- function(file_path) {
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  
  data <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  cat("--- Data Loaded Successfully ---\n")
  print(glimpse(data))
  
  cat("\n--- First 6 Rows ---\n")
  print(head(data))
  
  return(data)
}

# Call the function
my_data <- load_and_inspect("unsd-citypopulation-year-both.csv")

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 4.3. The “Query” Function (The Core of the Task)
# -----------------------------

top_cities_by_year <- function(data, year_value, n = 10) {
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(Year = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Year)))
  
  result <- data %>%
    filter(Year == year_value, !is.na(Value)) %>%
    select(City, `Country or Area`, Year, Population = Value) %>%
    arrange(desc(Population)) %>%
    slice_head(n = n)
  
  return(result)
}

# Call the function
top_10_latest <- top_cities_by_year(my_data, max(as.numeric(my_data$Year), na.rm = TRUE), n = 10)
top_10_latest

```

```{r}

# -----------------------------
# 4.4. The “Reporting” Function
# -----------------------------

generate_report <- function(data, city_name) {
  
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(Year = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Year)))
  
  city_data <- data %>%
    filter(City == city_name)
  
  if (nrow(city_data) == 0) {
    cat("No records found for city:", city_name, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  avg_pop <- mean(city_data$Value, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_pop <- max(city_data$Value, na.rm = TRUE)
  min_pop <- min(city_data$Value, na.rm = TRUE)
  years_range <- paste(min(city_data$Year), "to", max(city_data$Year))
  record_count <- nrow(city_data)
  
  cat("----------------------------------\n")
  cat("   Population Report for:", city_name, "\n")
  cat("----------------------------------\n")
  cat("Number of records:", record_count, "\n")
  cat("Year range:", years_range, "\n")
  cat("Average population:", round(avg_pop, 2), "\n")
  cat("Maximum population:", max_pop, "\n")
  cat("Minimum population:", min_pop, "\n")
  cat("----------------------------------\n\n")
}

# Call the function for two cities
generate_report(my_data, "TOKYO")
generate_report(my_data, "LONDON")

```
